label: Cookbook
description: A cookbook people actually cook from: chapters, recipes, technique, photography.

prompts.voice:
YOU ARE WRITING A COOKBOOK THAT PEOPLE COOK FROM, and read in bed.
Two things at once: every recipe must actually work at the stove, and every page
must be worth reading when nobody is cooking.

ABSOLUTE RULES OF VOICE
- Write to someone standing in their kitchen. Second person, present tense, calm.
- Quantities are exact and in both metric and cups. Times are ranges, never a
  single number, because pans and ovens differ.
- Say what it should look, sound and smell like at each step. "Until the edges
  lace and the middle still wobbles" beats "until done".
- Name the failure before it happens: what splits, what seizes, what burns, and
  what to do when it does.
- No preamble about the author's childhood unless it changes how the dish is made.
- Never invent a tradition, a provenance or a nutritional claim. If a dish's
  history is contested, say it is contested.
prompts.pillars:
The book as a whole must cover all six. Individual pages pick one or two.
1. TECHNIQUE - the movement of hands and heat: what you are actually doing and why.
2. INGREDIENT - what the thing is, how to choose it, when it is at its best.
3. ORIGIN - where the dish comes from, honestly, including where that is disputed.
4. SCIENCE - what the heat, acid, salt, fat or time is doing chemically.
5. VARIATION - the same dish done another way, and what changes.
6. TROUBLESHOOTING - what goes wrong, why, and the fix.
prompts.plan:
{{voice}}

BOOK: "{{title}}" - {{subject}}{{angleSuffix}}
THESIS: {{thesis}}
EXTENT: exactly {{extent}} pages.
{{notes}}

RESEARCH:
{{research}}

Build the table of contents.

STRUCTURE LAW (non-negotiable):
- p1 is the title page. p2 is the introduction: the argument, in the author's voice.
- Then chapters. A chapter opens with a chapter-opener page and groups dishes that
  share a technique or a moment of the day - never an arbitrary split.
- A recipe page carries exactly one recipe. A recipe never continues onto another page:
  if it will not fit, plan it as a recipe-spread instead.
- Put a technique or science page near the first recipe that needs it, not in an
  appendix nobody reads.
- End with an index page.
- Density: R = a full recipe, N = narrative or technique prose, I = index or reference.

Page types available: {{archetypes}}

Return ONLY JSON:
{
  "sections":[{"n":1,"label":"chapter name, printed","question":"the chapter opener line",
               "colour":"the chapter's colour world in words","from":3,"to":18}],
  "pages":[{"n":1,"title":"the page's own title","type":"one of the types above",
            "density":"R|N|I","section":0,
            "pillar":"technique|ingredient|origin|science|variation|troubleshooting|none",
            "premise":"one sentence: what THIS page does that no other page does"}]
}
Exactly {{extent}} page entries, n from 1 to {{extent}}, in order.
section 0 = front and back matter.
